songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line
Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

ai_show_review.summary: High-energy second set with standout Bertha solo and soaring Stella Blue
ai_show_review.blurb: The band delivers a high‑energy performance highlighted by Jerry’s blistering solo on “Bertha” and Phil’s driving bass throughout the second set. Standout renditions include “Stella Blue,” the “Not Fade Away” medley, and “Friend Of The Devil.” Recording quality is poor – vocals are low, keyboards nearly absent, and the mix muddy – but the playing shines through.
ai_show_review.review: The Dead on November 12, 1972 at Soldiers' and Sailors' Memorial Hall brought a burst of momentum that kept the audience moving despite a less‑than‑ideal tape. Set one rolls out familiar classics with tight interplay, but it’s the second set where the night truly clicks: Jerry launches into a machine‑gun pace solo on “Bertha,” while Phil drops bombs with a thick, propulsive bass line. The group then rides through “Tennessee Jed” and “Playing In The Band,” before slipping into a soulful “Stella Blue” that feels almost reverent in the sparse mix. A highlight is the rolling “Not Fade Away” medley – weaving “He's Gone,” two takes of “Not Fade Away,” and “Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad” – that showcases the band’s relentless groove even as keyboards fade into the background. Although the soundboard capture suffers from low vocals, missing keys, and an over‑saturated bass, the core performance remains compelling, offering a vivid snapshot of the Fall ’72 lineup in full swing.

best_recording.reason: Only available soundboard; despite muddy mix it captures the band’s tight playing and the high‑energy second‑set flow.

key_highlights: Jerry’s machine‑gun pace solo on “Bertha” stands out as a showcase of his lead work.
Stella Blue delivers an emotive, soaring performance that cuts through the thin mix.
The Not Fade Away medley drives the latter half of set two with relentless groove.
Strong rhythmic foundation from Phil and Bill keeps everything locked in despite missing keyboards.

band_performance.Jerry: Blistering machine‑gun pace licks and a killer solo on “Bertha”; guitar shines despite the sparse mix.
band_performance.Phil: Drops bombs with a great groove, especially on “Bertha”; bass tone occasionally over‑saturated but drives the band forward.
band_performance.Bob: Exquisite interplay with Jerry and Phil; rhythm work comes through clearly thanks to the reduced keyboard presence.
band_performance.Brent: Keyboards (Keith) are largely missing from the mix, making his contributions hard to hear.
band_performance.Billy: Bill’s drumming is solid but often buried in the mix; occasional sections feature only drums audible.
